content:
Dear Hiring Team at Halden Pay,

I am applying for the Senior Data Engineer – Data Platform position. I have nine years of experience building and operating production data platforms across logistics, e-commerce and payments, with hands-on experience in Python, SQL, Airflow, dbt and cloud data warehouses. Halden Pay’s focus on a shared platform and reusable frameworks is a strong match for the work I have been doing.

At Lukovac Freight Hub, I own ingestion and orchestration for a central platform with approximately 140 Airflow DAGs, and migrated more than 420 warehouse models to dbt with tests. That work reduced the nightly build time from 5 hours 10 minutes to 1 hour 35 minutes. I have also introduced JSON Schema data contracts and CI checks between product and data teams, and built Kafka pipelines processing around 30 million events per day. These experiences have taught me to focus on reliable platform foundations, data quality and engineering practices that can be reused across teams.

My experience at Kovalent Pay is directly relevant to Halden Pay’s business. I built PySpark jobs on AWS EMR to reconcile bank settlement files against internal ledgers, processing approximately 1.2 TB of raw files daily, and helped reduce month-end manual reconciliation work from around three days to four hours. I also designed a Redshift dimensional warehouse for finance and risk teams. Alongside this cloud data platform experience, I have contributed two merged pull requests to an Airflow provider and presented on data contracts at a regional data meetup. I hold an MSc in Computer Science and an AWS Certified Data Engineer – Associate certification.

I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience operating data platforms, improving data quality and building reusable tooling could support Halden Pay’s Data Platform team and its business clients.

Kind regards,
Lena Varga-Holm

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, concise cover letter with clear relevance to the Senior Data Engineer – Data Platform role. It uses credible metrics, demonstrates production-scale platform work, and connects the candidate’s payments experience to Halden Pay’s fintech context. The progression from platform ownership at Lukovac to reconciliation and warehouse work at Kovalent Pay is logical and professional. The main opportunity is to make a few role requirements more explicit, particularly day-to-day platform operations, query or warehouse optimisation, data quality governance, and collaboration with platform users. No unsupported skills or experiences were detected.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter is ATS-friendly: it uses standard headings-free prose, readable paragraphs, conventional text formatting, and relevant keywords including Python, SQL, Airflow, dbt, Kafka, PySpark, AWS EMR, Redshift, data quality, data contracts, and dimensional warehouse. AI screening probability is high because the document contains specific scale and outcome evidence rather than generic claims. Keyword coverage could be improved by explicitly using supported job-ad terms such as “production data platform,” “cloud data warehouse,” “data modelling,” “data quality standards,” “reusable frameworks,” “open-source,” and “query optimisation.” Do not add Google Cloud, BigQuery, GKE, Cloud Run, graph modelling, or Portuguese because they are not supported by the candidate information.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document shows a strong match for production data platforms, cloud warehouses, Airflow, dbt, Python, SQL, dimensional modelling, comparable cloud infrastructure, open-source practices, and payments-domain work. It also demonstrates ownership, operational reliability, mentoring, and reusable engineering practices that fit Halden Pay’s Together, Ownership and Pace values. The candidate’s AWS experience is a valid comparable-cloud match, although it is not Google Cloud. The letter does not explicitly mention query optimisation on large datasets, data governance or access policies, collaboration with data scientists/analytics/BI colleagues, or day-to-day on-call operations, despite the candidate material supporting some closely related evidence. Graph modelling and Portuguese are genuine gaps in the candidate material and should not be presented as document defects.
critique.improvement_instructions:

1. In the second paragraph, after the sentence about owning approximately 140 Airflow DAGs, add the supported operational detail: “I also participate in the data platform on-call rotation, helping keep production ingestion and orchestration reliable day to day.” This makes the job’s “operate” requirement explicit.
2. In the second paragraph, strengthen the platform-quality alignment by adding the candidate’s measurable data-quality result after the sentence about JSON Schema data contracts: “The associated CI checks reduced broken-pipeline incidents from approximately nine to two per month.” This is more concrete than the current general reference to data quality.
3. In the third paragraph, make the comparable-cloud and data-modelling requirements explicit by changing “I also designed a Redshift dimensional warehouse for finance and risk teams” to “I also designed a Redshift cloud data warehouse using dimensional modelling, with more than 30 fact and dimension tables for finance and risk teams.”
4. In the second paragraph, add the supported warehouse-performance evidence after the dbt build-time result: “I also reduced Snowflake spend from approximately $38,000 to $24,000 per month through warehouse sizing, auto-suspend and removal of unused tables.” This demonstrates scale and optimisation without claiming unsupported specific SQL-query tuning.

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is professional, credible, and well aligned with the Senior Data Engineer – Data Platform role. It uses strong quantified evidence: 140 Airflow DAGs, 420+ dbt models, build-time reduction, Snowflake cost reduction, 30 million events per day, and reconciliation improvements. The progression from platform engineering at Lukovac to payments experience at Kovalent Pay is particularly relevant to Halden Pay. The main content weakness is density: the second paragraph contains several major achievements and could be easier to scan if divided or tightened. The closing also repeats “operating data platforms,” and the letter does not explicitly connect the candidate’s experience to advanced SQL/query optimisation or defining governance/access standards as clearly as it could.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter is ATS-friendly in plain text: it uses standard headings implicitly through paragraph structure, conventional role terminology, and relevant keywords including data platform, Python, SQL, Airflow, dbt, Snowflake, Kafka, PySpark, AWS, Redshift, dimensional modelling, data quality, CI checks, and open-source contributions. It contains no tables, graphics, unusual symbols, or parsing-risk formatting. AI screening probability is high because the letter includes quantified scope, relevant fintech experience, production operations, cloud data platforms, and open-source activity. ATS alignment could be improved modestly by explicitly using the job description’s terms “production data platforms,” “cloud data warehouses at scale,” “data modelling,” “query optimisation,” “reusable frameworks,” and “open-source practices,” but only where supported by the candidate’s information.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document shows a strong match for the core role. It demonstrates designing, building, and operating a production data platform; Airflow and dbt; Python; SQL; cloud data warehouses; AWS as a comparable cloud; dimensional modelling; data quality; fintech/payments experience; open-source contributions; and professional English. The candidate’s experience with Snowflake, Redshift, AWS EMR, S3, Docker, and CI checks is relevant to Halden Pay’s Google Cloud-based stack even though Google Cloud itself is not listed in the candidate information. The letter also supports the company’s Ownership and Pace themes through on-call responsibility, incident reduction, cost reduction, and faster build times, although it does not explicitly name those values. The candidate material does not show graph modelling or Portuguese; these are gaps in the candidate profile rather than defects in the letter. The letter also does not provide strong evidence of access policies or broad governance ownership, so it should not imply those capabilities without additional supporting experience.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR, HIGH-VALUE IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the opening paragraph, replace the general sentence “I have nine years of experience building and operating production data platforms across logistics, e-commerce and payments, with hands-on experience in Python, SQL, Airflow, dbt and cloud data warehouses” with a more job-specific version that uses the ad’s terminology: “I have nine years of experience designing, building and operating production data platforms and cloud data warehouses at scale, using Python, SQL, Airflow, dbt and AWS.” This is supported by the CV and improves ATS alignment.

2. In the second paragraph, split the current long paragraph after the sentence ending “day to day.” Keep the platform operations and dbt results in the first paragraph, then begin a new paragraph with “I also reduced Snowflake spend...” This will make the evidence easier for a recruiter and an AI screener to scan without changing the substance.

3. In the paragraph describing Lukovac, revise “migrated more than 420 warehouse models to dbt with tests” to “migrated more than 420 warehouse models to dbt, with tests on every model.” This matches the associated CV and original candidate information more precisely.

4. In the paragraph describing the Kovalent Pay experience, change “designed a Redshift cloud data warehouse using dimensional modelling” to “designed a Redshift cloud data warehouse using dimensional modelling, with more than 30 fact and dimension tables for finance and risk teams.” This restores the strongest modelling evidence already present in the associated CV.

5. Where accurate based on the existing evidence, add one concise sentence after the Snowflake cost-reduction result: “This work included improving warehouse efficiency and reducing processing time and cost on large analytical workloads.” Do not call this “query optimisation” unless the candidate can substantiate query-level optimisation specifically; the current evidence supports workload and warehouse optimisation more clearly.

6. In the final paragraph, remove the duplicated phrase in “operating data platforms, defining data quality checks, operating production data platforms and building reusable frameworks and tooling.” Replace it with: “I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience operating production data platforms, defining data quality checks, and building reusable tooling and frameworks could support Halden Pay’s Data Platform team.” This is cleaner and avoids repetition while remaining supported by the candidate’s internal Python library, dbt migration, CI checks, and platform work.

7. In the final paragraph, replace “its business clients” with “analysts, data scientists and product teams” only if the candidate wants to mirror the role description and is comfortable presenting their experience as supporting those audiences. Otherwise, retain the current wording; the associated CV clearly supports analysts and finance/risk teams, but does not explicitly document direct work with data scientists.
